issues.legal_issue: Minor inconsistencies and delayed testimony in eyewitness accounts do not undermine the prosecution case when the witnesses consistently identify the person who inflicted the fatal blow.
A medical opinion that the injuries could have resulted from a fall does not outweigh corroborated eyewitness testimony when the defence account is unsupported and internally inconsistent.
The High Court was justified in reversing the acquittal where the prosecution evidence was reliable and no material evidence had been misread or ignored.
